hypothesis: At the current 192-thread CTA/tile setting, replacing 28-byte staged Particle records with 16-byte source records reduces dynamic shared memory from 5,376 to 3,072 bytes while retaining the same one-target-per-thread mapping, source order, and barriers. Compact staging was measured as valid and faster at 128 threads, but it is not known whether the benefit carries over to 192 threads or offsets the staging costs; the official measurements should test that assumption.
notes: This changes the source record layout while preserving the selected parent's 192-thread CTA/tile mapping. The compact record occupies 3,072 bytes per CTA, below the parent's 5,376-byte allocation. Historical timings are context only; no result is claimed for this candidate.
transformations: Keep block and items_per_block at 192, with exactly one target per thread and source tiles of 192 particles.
Stage only source x, y, z, and mass in a 16-byte shared-memory record, reducing the allocation to 3,072 bytes while preserving ascending source interaction order and force arithmetic.
Retain both CTA-wide barriers, partial source-tile handling, and target/output bounds checks.
